To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the algorithm of Fossaier and Lin can be modified in several ways that allow large computation savings and significant decoding speedup without much error performance degradation

(1) a new probabilistic list is proposed for the reprocessing order in order-i algorithms; (2) a probabilistic stopping test is proposed for the order-0 algorithm; (3) an adaptive coset decoding is proposed; (4) an order-i algorithm for |u| is proposed.

the Fossorier-Lin algorithm can be made much more efficient by using a reduced list of codewords and/or a stopping criterion and/or a reprocessing order based on the structure of a code, or a combination of these techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of computationally efficient decoding algorithms for linear block codes.
the development of computationally efficient soft-decision algorithms for the decoding of linear block error-correcting codes, with a particular emphasis on the decoding of |u|u|u+v|.
the design of efficient decoding algorithms for a wide range of linear block codes
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is a very powerful tool for the decoding of a wide variety of linear codes.
the proposed improvements allow the algorithm to be used with a large variety of codes with a significant gain in decoding speed and/or in memory requirements with little performance degradation
the proposed modifications are very useful in practice and that the algorithm can be used with a wide variety of codes and decoding strategies
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithm provides an efficient soft-decision decoder which is able to take advantage of the code structure.
the most reliable basis algorithm of Fossorer and Lin has been improved in such a way that its performance and efficiency are comparable to that of the Viterbi algorithm. (7 pages)
the proposed modifications allow a significant reduction of the average number of operations per codeword, and thus, a large speedup in the implementation of the algorithm of Fossoier and Lin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given decoding algorithm, the choice of the reprocessing order can significantly affect its performance, in terms of error performance and decoding speed.
the decoding complexity of linear block codes can be significantly decreased without a noticeable performance loss.
the Fossorier-Lin algorithm is a powerful tool that can be adapted in several ways to achieve a very efficient and effective decoding scheme.
